title: Introduce dependency-aware span pruner and Token Economics Explorer dashboard
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context and motivation: Customer SLO incidents surfaced a recurring pattern where high token costs were concentrated in downstream model stages that were only reachable through specific dependency branches in multi-stage pipelines. Existing span sampling and pruning removed a lot of noise but also discarded spans that were essential for cost attribution. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a dependency-aware span pruner service that retains spans flagged as cost-sensitive or dependency-critical while aggressively pruning repetitive housekeeping spans; and 2) a Token Economics Explorer dashboard that surfaces per-invocation cost breakdowns along dependency edges (stage->stage) so SREs and platform engineers can identify expensive call paths.

What this change does (single-line summary): Adds a span-pruner microservice with an adaptive rule engine and a Grafana/JSON dashboard for detailed token-cost-by-dependency visualization plus small exporters and tests.

Design and implementation notes: The span pruner runs as an observability sidecar (configurable) and applies a two-pass algorithm: a lightweight dependency classifier during ingestion and a short-term retention policy that keeps spans matching dependency heuristics or cost delta signals. Rules are prioritized: explicit cost-anchors > warmed-kv-prefetch > dependency-root spans > sampled debug spans. The pruner exposes metrics for kept/pruned ratio, recycler throughput, and rule-evaluation latency. The Token Economics Explorer ingests token-cost rollups and joins them with span-edge metadata to present: token-cost by edge, cumulative percent of total cost by path, and a small sparkline of per-minute cost velocity.

Files touched (high-level): observability/span_pruner/service.go, observability/span_pruner/config.yaml, observability/span_pruner/rules.md, observability/exporters/token_cost_exporter.go, dashboards/token_economics_explorer.json, dashboards/examples/token_econ_sample_queries.promql, docs/observability/token-economics.md, tests/span_pruner_integration_test.go, pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go.

Commits summary: feat(span-pruner): initial pruner service, adds rule engine and basic metrics; feat(exporter): token cost exporter and Prometheus integration; docs: token economics playbook and dashboard walkthrough; test: integration tests for retention invariants; ci: add workflow for dashboard linting.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for rule evaluation (coverage ~92% on new packages). Integration test simulates a 3-stage pipeline and asserts that spans contributing >85% of token-cost on a path are retained. CI runs: ci/build (pass), ci/unit-tests (pass), ci/integration-tests (flaky first run, rerun and pass), ci/lint (pass), ci/dashboard-lint (pass). The integration test required a small timing tweak (increased pruner retention window in test) after an early flaky failure, which is reflected in the final commits.

Review notes and trade-offs: The pruner defaults to opt-in via new observability.sidecar.enabled flag to avoid any surprise data loss. We intentionally favor keeping cost-significant spans to preserve billing triangulation at the cost of slightly higher observability volume for flagged customers. Rule engine is pluggable; future work includes an ML-based dependency classifier and a policy UI in Console.

Rollout plan: 1) feature gated rollout to internal staging tenants for 48h; 2) canary to 5% of hostings for 72h with monitoring (kept/pruned ratio, token-cost-matched-traces percent); 3) global opt-in release. A rollback toggle (observability.sidecar.mode=passthrough) is included.

Backward compatibility and migration: No schema changes to existing spans. Dashboard uses new token_cost exporter metrics but falls back to legacy rollups if unavailable. Documentation includes migration steps for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Open items / follow-ups: implement configurable sampling budget per-tenant, add span-anchored log-snapshot export for high-cost invocations, and dashboard drilldown from path to raw trace.

Related tickets: ENG-6123 (design doc), PM-211 (product acceptance criteria).

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: The retention heuristics look sensible, but can you add a guard to avoid retaining long tails for noisy tenants? Suggested a per-tenant max-kept-spans cap.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Added a per-tenant retention cap config (observability.sidecar.max_kept_spans). See config.yaml and tests for bounds enforcement.
Elena Petrova: Dashboard queries look heavy — consider adding pre-aggregated edges in the token_cost_exporter to reduce Grafana query time.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Exporter now emits token_cost_edge_sum per minute (sampled) and a small cache to serve dashboard queries; added explanation in docs.
Samir Patel: Integration test was flaky on CI initially — was this due to timing? Please document why retention window was increased.
Aisha Kapoor: Yes, the pruner's short-term retention window of 30s caused race with test harness. Increased to 60s in test and added a stable clock abstraction for deterministic runs.
build_logs_summary: Initial integration run failed due to timing; added deterministic clock in test and reran CI. All checks green on final run.
release_notes: Add dependency-aware span pruner sidecar (opt-in) and Token Economics Explorer dashboard for per-path token cost attribution. Includes exporter metrics and integration tests. Feature gated behind observability.sidecar.enabled.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature via observability.sidecar.enabled in config. Watch metrics: span_pruner_kept_total, span_pruner_pruned_total, token_cost_edge_sum, pruner_rule_eval_latency_ms. Rollback by setting observability.sidecar.mode=passthrough.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: default opt-in reduces blast radius; risk primarily in increased observability volume for tenants with many flagged dependency paths. QA validated retention invariants.
manual_verification_steps: Run the provided integration harness under tests/span_pruner_integration_test.go
Open dashboards/token_economics_explorer.json in Grafana and verify per-path cost matches test harness outputs
Flip observability.sidecar.mode to passthrough to confirm rollback behavior
